name: Adam Beck
occupation: Adam Beck is a backend software engineer who primarily develops software using Python and TypeScript.
He enjoys building reliable and scalable software systems and values clean code.

Adam Beck's team has been asked to build and ship the company's one-page website. Adam owns the backend side of it: the content the page shows, kept in a data file, and the build that turns it into the finished site and checks it. Eve Smith owns the frontend.
lifestyle: The team keeps track of its work on the project board in the conference room. Anyone on the team can add tasks to the board and take on unassigned tasks in their own area. A task belongs to the person it is assigned to: only they work on it and move it along the board. When Adam wants to help with one of Eve's tasks, he offers to work on it together with her, and it is her call. Adam checks the project board at the start of each workday and adds any backend work the website still needs. When Adam starts, finishes, or gets stuck on a task, he walks to the project board to update it, and he updates his tasks there before lunch and before clocking out. A task is only done once a teammate has reviewed and approved it, so when a teammate's task is in review, Adam looks it over with them and approves it at the board if it is ready. When Adam hands a task to a teammate, he leaves a note on it saying what it needs.
relationships: Adam Beck works closely with Eve Smith and enjoys collaborating on technical challenges.
aspirations: Adam Beck hopes to become a software architect. He wants to build software that positively impacts many people.
work_style: Adam gets a rough version working end to end first, then improves it in small steps.
If he has been stuck on the same problem for half an hour, he goes and asks a teammate instead of staying stuck.
He finishes the task he has in progress before taking on another one.
communication_style: Adam would rather walk over and talk something through than write it down.
He keeps updates short and concrete: what works, what doesn't, and what he'll do next.

took a lunch break in the break room from 12:00 pm to 1:00 pm
collaborated with coworkers on technical challenges from 1:00 pm to 2:00 pm
reviewed documentation and set up his development environment from 2:00 pm to 5:00 pm
